value.statement: If the nonproperness curve S_F of a plane Keller map is connected then F is étale-maximal; equivalently, non-maximality forces S_F to be disconnected. value.name: Two-nodal-fiber theorem

research.author: packet 2026-09-14: LLM-derived, no claim-specific human check, no Lean kernel build
research.reason: highest-priority human audit; never to be described as Assi's theorem

semantics: KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmaximal_implies_exactlyTwoNodalFibers: core; audit unapproved; the two-nodal-fiber derivation from KG-EM07, KG-EM08, KG-EM09 and Assi's equinodal theorem, free of any Lean hole; it carries KG-EM07's two assumed prerequisites, so the claim is not verified by this
value.statement: If a plane Keller map is not étale-maximal then S_F = C_0 ⊔ C_1 with C_i = V(h − a_i) the two exceptional rational members of a noncoordinate one-place pencil; each C_i is rational with one place at infinity, and both have the same positive number of affine singular points, all ordinary transverse nodes. The classification of the two fibers is Assi's; the reduction from Keller non-maximality to it is the project's.

value.name: Perfect monodromy in the residual non-maximal case

research.author: packet 2026-09-14: LLM-derived, no claim-specific human check, no Lean kernel build

semantics: KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmaximal_implies_perfectMonodromy: core; audit verified; the group-theoretic step of PM-1: perfectness follows once the nodal vanishing cycles are assumed to generate the sheet monodromy with each generator a ratio of conjugate branch inertias. Those are the audit's own two load-bearing points and both are assumed here, so the claim is not verified by this
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.conjugateRatio_eq_commutatorElement: core; audit verified; a ratio of conjugate elements is a commutator
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.perfect_of_conjugateRatio_generators: core; audit verified; a group generated by ratios of conjugate elements is perfect
value.statement: Assuming KG-EM10, the sheet-monodromy group of a non-étale-maximal plane Keller map is perfect. The monodromy around a nodal vanishing cycle is σ_+σ_-^{-1} with σ_± conjugate branch-inertia permutations, hence trivial in the abelianization; the load-bearing points are that the vanishing cycles generate H_1 of the generic Assi fiber and that the pulled-back cover's monodromy over that fiber surjects onto the full sheet monodromy.
